post.summary: Complete QR payment with signed transaction
post.description: Broadcasts the signed UserOp, or submits the signed Rain withdrawal via the session key, first; the Manteca payment is created only once the USDC mined at the QR deposit address and is claimed for this attempt. A payment that fails after that is recorded and its USDC refunded. One payment lock is funded at most once: while another attempt for the lock is unresolved the answer is 409 FUNDING_PENDING_CONFIRMATION, and once that attempt moved money and is final it is 409 QR_PAYMENT_LOCK_USED. Neither sends anything.

post.summary: Resolve a PIX key to its owner
post.description: Returns the owner's name and masked CPF/CNPJ for a PIX key before the user pays it. 404 PAYMENT_DESTINATION_NOT_FOUND means the key does not exist. 502 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, 429 and 400 MANTECA_KYC_REQUIRED mean no name is available; the client pays without one.

post.summary: Save a PIX key to the address book
post.description: Saves a PIX key as one of the user's bank accounts, named with the label. The API decides whose key it is, once, with the directory lookup the Pix withdrawal uses, through the user's open Pix withdraw route: the user's own key is saved as a withdrawal destination; any other key, or any key while that route is closed, is saved as a recipient (isPixRecipient) for Send → Bank, never offered as a withdrawal destination. A recipient needs Pix payment eligibility; an own key needs only the open route. Where the open route's provider pays any key (Avenia), that provider saves the key with the holder and bank its lookup validated, own key or recipient; the lookup's refusals (those of POST /pix/key) answer instead. Saving a key the user already has renames it.
